newsitem.title: UK: UK Lib-Lab coalition said possible, but unlikely.
newsitem.headline: UK Lib-Lab coalition said possible, but unlikely.

text.p: The leader of Britain's minority Liberal Democrats said on Monday that a coalition with the opposition Labour Party was possible, but unlikely.

Asked on BBC radio whether he could see himself supporting Labour leader Tony Blair consistently in the House of Commons, Ashdown replied: "All the options are open. Nothing is ruled in, nothing is ruled out."
He added: "Is it possible we will do what you suggest? Yes. Is it likely? No."

Alex Carlile, one of the other 25 Liberal Democrat MPs said on Sunday, the first day of the party's annual cinference in the southern resort of Brighton, that Ashdown should seek a coalition with Labour provided it was prepared to implement some Liberal policies.
